title: Calculate Brownian-particle parameters from literature data
action: Using the coarse-graining radius R_B = 2.25 nm, water zero-field viscosity η_0 = 8.9×10⁻⁴ Pa·s, the experimentally observed Debye-like relaxation time of 29.5 ns, the field-induced free-energy shift from Zong et al., and molecular dipole estimates, compute the Brownian particle concentration c_B, number of molecules per segment n_B, effective Brownian dipole magnitude p_0B, rotational friction ζ_B^r, shape anisotropy δ_B, coupling factor χ̄, parameter α₁, and background fluid viscosity η_f. Save the computed parameters as structured evidence.
description: Converts published experimental and MD data into numerical parameters for the coarse-grained Brownian-particle model.

title: Compute viscoelectric coefficient f_v
action: Take the Brownian-particle parameters from the previous step. For the experimental conditions of Jin et al. (T=298 K, bulk concentration c₀=0.08 mM, electrode potentials V₁=-150 mV and V₂=100 mV, gap L=57.5 nm), solve the 1D Poisson–Boltzmann equation to obtain the surface electric field E_s. Compute the correction factors L_E = (E_s/E₀)² and L_m using the MLB model expressions. Then compute f_vB = c_B ζ_B^r χ̄ β² p_0B²/(315 η_0) and the final viscoelectric coefficient f_v = L_E L_m f_vB. Save the result and the intermediates to the output file.
description: Stores the computed viscoelectric coefficient and intermediate quantities.
